title: Add playbook-visualizer quickstart with live contract editor and step inspector
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary: Adds a new quickstart that combines a lightweight playbook visualizer, an inline "live" contract editor for tools, and a step inspector that surfaces telemetry/trace snippets. Motivation: authoring and debugging RAG playbooks is still split between static YAML/JSON and separate contract validators. This quickstart (playbook-visualizer) provides a single local development flow that speeds iteration: visual feedback for step ordering, simple drag-reorder, contract validation in-place, and an inspector pane showing the request/response, KV-cache usage, and telemetry markers emitted during a simulated run.

What this PR contains: single continuous description and checklist below. Files include a compact React-based visualizer (src/ui), a minimal TypeScript adapter that runs playbooks against a local light runner (src/runner), a devcontainer and docker-compose for local simulation, docs site quickstart page (docs/quickstarts/playbook-visualizer.md), CI smoke workflow ( .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml ) to run the local runner in headless mode, and a small set of example playbooks and tool contracts (examples/). The UI is intentionally dependency-light to keep the quickstart fast to clone and run.

Checklist: - [x] Visualizer UI + step inspector implementation - [x] Live contract editor with inline linting & schema hints - [x] Local playbook runtime shim (no GPU required) - [x] Devcontainer and docker-compose quickstart - [x] Docs quickstart page and code snippets - [x] CI smoke workflow + unit tests for contract lint rules - [x] Telemetry samples and small synthetic run corpus for demos

How it works (high-level): The visualizer consumes a playbook JSON schema and renders steps as nodes. Each node has a contract editor that is backed by the same JSON-schema-based validator used in our production tool-contract linter. The runner simulates calls to tool adapters (stubbed network responses) and emits compact telemetry events. The step inspector subscribes to the runner over a websocket and shows the last 10 events for the selected step, KV cache hits/misses, and synthetic latency histograms. A local watch mode uses filesystem events to hot-reload playbooks and contracts in the browser for fast iteration.

Developer notes and usage: 1) Clone repo, cd quickstarts/playbook-visualizer 2) Start devcontainer (or run docker-compose up) to install and launch the UI and runner 3) Open http://localhost:3002 and pick an example playbook. Edit tool contracts inline and press "Validate". Validation errors appear in the contract panel and also as red badges on steps. 4) Press "Run (Simulate)" to execute a synthetic run; step inspector will stream events. 5) Use "Export" to generate a production-ready playbook.yaml that pins contract SHAs and a suggested rollout policy.

Testing and CI: The included workflow runs the runner in headless mode, executes a small set of example playbooks and asserts that exported playbooks pass the contract linter. Unit tests target contract validation rules (schema conformance, required fields, param typing) and the runner event semantics. CI output is lightweight to keep CI minutes low.

Changed areas / files (high level): src/ui/Visualizer.tsx - React visualizer and inspector; src/ui/ContractEditor.tsx - in-browser editor and lint integration; src/runner/sim-runner.ts - lightweight simulator; examples/sample-playbooks/*.json - three example playbooks demonstrating branching, tool-fallbacks and KV-cache reuse; docs/quickstarts/playbook-visualizer.md - step-by-step guide; .devcontainer/* and docker-compose.yml - local quickstart; .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml - CI smoke flow.

Commits (summary): 1) initial scaffold of visualizer and minimal runner; 2) add contract editor + schema integration; 3) wire telemetry stream & step inspector; 4) add examples and docs; 5) CI workflow and unit tests; 6) polish UX, keyboard shortcuts, and accessibility tweaks.

Review thread highlights: - Miguel: requested clearer error mapping between contract lint messages and step nodes (addressed in commit 4; lint markers now include node id and line preview). - Lina: asked for a smaller devcontainer image to reduce onboarding time; switched base to node:18-slim and moved heavy deps to optional layer (commit 5). - Samir: suggested adding a demonstration of prefix/KV cache reuse; added sample-playbooks/cache-reuse.json and instrumented the runner to surface cache hit ratio in the inspector. All reviewers approved after the fixes.

CI checks: - quickstart-smoke (passed) - unit (passed) - lint (passed) - accessibility-scan (warn -> fixed in follow-up commit)

Merge outcome: squash and merge by Lina Chen. Changelog/release notes: Adds a new quickstart: "Playbook Visualizer + Live Contract Editor" (developer-facing tool to speed RAG playbook authoring, validation and debugging). This is non-breaking and intended as a local developer experience; no runtime or API surface changes to hosted Redwood product.

Follow-ups planned: (1) Add a compact rollout export that integrates with Redwood Console rollout API (ENG-2380). (2) Expand sample corpus with multi-tenant examples. (3) Post-merge: schedule a docs-site guided video walkthrough and short webinar for developer community.

If you'd like to run the quickstart locally and give UX feedback, see docs/quickstarts/playbook-visualizer.md for step-by-step commands and troubleshooting notes.

release_notes: Add developer quickstart: Playbook Visualizer with Live Contract Editor and Step Inspector — local dev flow for RAG playbook authoring and debugging; non-breaking; docs included.
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally keeps the runner dependency-free (no GPU) and uses stubbed tool adapters. When evolving to a production export path, we will add an opt-in integration that signs exported contracts against the model registry. See follow-up ENG-2380.
